newsitem.title: USA: Heinz ends talks for Bumble Bee tuna.
newsitem.headline: Heinz ends talks for Bumble Bee tuna.

text.p: H.J. Heinz Co said it terminated its quest to acquire the production plants of Bumble Bee tuna, a move analysts said was not surprising because it would have given the food giant too much market share.

The Pittsburgh-based food manufacturer, which owns Star-Kist tuna, and Questor Partners Fund LP, an investor group, said in statement they terminated discussions with Bumble Bee Seafoods Inc, a unit of Unicord Public Co Ltd of Bangkok.
Heinz officials were not available for comment. A news release did not explain why discussions were halted, but analysts said the potential transaction was under close scrutiny by the FTC.
Had the transaction gone through, Questor would have purchased Bumble Bee tuna, and in turn would have sold its three production plants to Heinz.
The transaction had been valued at more than $200 million.
"It was not a surprise (that talks were terminated,") said analyst Laurie Feldman at Bear Stearns.
"Had (Heinz) purchased just the supply rights, they would have had 85 percent of all the tuna volume in the world, Feldman said. "That's just too much."
"The FTC is not stupid. Heinz has tried to purchase Bumble Bee several times before," Feldman added.
Star-Kist tuna already is the world's leading tuna producer in terms of sales.
Feldman said Heinz decided to terminate discussions after receiving a "second request for information from the FTC."
She said she did not know when the company received that request. -- Pittsburgh newsroom 412-471-7088
